name: Fashion editorial photography
summary: Planned pictures of clothes, bodies and attitude for a magazine page. Light, set, pose and edit are all designed, so that the image sells a world and not only a garment.

philosophy.core_thesis: Fashion sells a feeling before it sells a thing, so the photograph builds the whole world around the clothes.
design_principles: Use an 85mm to 135mm lens at f/5.6 to f/11, so that the body keeps its proportion and the clothes stay sharp.
Light with one large source: a 1.2m to 2m soft box or a beauty dish, with a key-to-fill ratio of 3:1 to 8:1.
Pose from the hip and the neck: make long lines, and give the hands a task.
Choose a set, a location or a colour sweep that carries the story, and place the model in it with 40–60% negative space.
Retouch skin to a natural texture, and grade for a clear mood: pastel, hard flash or film noir.
Shoot 300 to 1000 frames for 6 to 12 pages.
anti_patterns: Flat catalogue light with a stiff front pose
Heavy beauty-filter skin and plastic textures
Shots with no set, no story and no direction
Stock poses that ignore the garment
Competing props that hide the clothes

composition.framing: Vertical and clean; the figure is a strong line, often cropped at the knee or the hand.
composition.viewpoint: Waist to eye height, sometimes low for power; the camera is square to the body.
composition.geometry: Long diagonals from a leg, an arm or a train; a set line cuts the figure.
composition.subject_placement: Off centre, with 40–60% negative space or a colour field for type.

principles.rule: Let 1 figure take 40–60% of the height; the eye goes to the face and then to the garment.
Leave 40–60% of the page empty for a title or a pull quote.
Use asymmetric balance: figure on one third, an object or a shadow on the other.
Use 1 to 3 diagonals, a leg, an arm or a train, that run to the face.
Set 60% in one field, 30% in the garment hue and 10% in an accent such as lip or shoe.

light.quality: A large soft source for beauty, or a hard flash for edge; the light is shaped on purpose.
light.direction: 45° front-side and 30° above, with a fill card at the opposite side.
light.time_of_day: Studio, any hour; on location, the hour before sunset

lens_and_camera.format: Medium format or digital full frame; tethered to a screen
lens_and_camera.focus: Focus on the near eye; keep the garment inside the depth of field at f/8.
lens_and_camera.support: Tripod or handheld with a monolight
equipment: medium format or full frame body

colour_and_grade.treatment: Clean colour with a chosen cast: pastel and bright, or deep and moody, with natural skin.
grade_recipe: Set the white balance at 5600K and tint +3.
Set the black point at 2% and the white point at 98%.
Apply +20% midtone contrast with a soft S-curve.
Lift saturation by +15% but protect skin with a skin-tone mask at −10%.
Retouch blemishes only; keep pores at 70% of the original texture.
Add a clean grain, amount 8%, to unify the retouch.
colour_and_grade.grain: Light and even: a film-like layer that hides retouch seams

subjects: set pieces and architecture as a stage
motion: a coat, a hair, a train
subject_and_staging.staging: Full. A team of 6 to 20 people: stylist, hair, make-up, set designer, art director and the maker.
subject_and_staging.direction: Give the model a character, a motion and a gaze; reshoot the pose in steps of 3 to 5 frames.

workflow: Tether to a screen and review each frame with the art director.
Select 3 to 5 frames per look from 300 to 1000 shots.
Retouch skin and fabric, and match colour across the spread.
Lay out with type, 40–60% negative space and a clean margin.
post_processing.output: A magazine spread or campaign image of 8×10 in at 300 dpi, with room for type.

emotion.target_response: Desire and aspiration: the viewer wants the world around the clothes.

use_cases: image prompts for styled studio scenes
avoid_when: The brief needs a candid or documentary feel.
The garment must be shown for fit and cut at true proportion only.

modifiers.how: Go on location with a 35mm lens, no flash and a found street; keep the model in motion at 1/250s.
Use one hard key at a ratio of 16:1, a black ground and a long shadow; shoot in black and white at f/4.

sources.title: Vince Aletti and others, Avedon Fashion 1944–2000 (Abrams, 2009)
Nathalie Herschdorfer, Models, Photographers, and the Art of Fashion Photography (Thames & Hudson, 2012)
